violation_type.title: Written Operational Policies - Parental Notifications (26 TAC §746.501(a)(6))
violation_type.typical_finding: Operational Policies did not state how they will notify parents.

finding_variants.text: Operational Policies did not state how they will notify parents.
This standard was evaluated as part of an investigation and found to be deficient. The operation did not follow their operational policy regarding parent notification of a child head injury.
It was found while reviewing the operation's Operation Policy that this was missing in their policy.

The operational policies were missing the following sections, (6)Procedures for parental notifications (9)Safe sleep policy for infants (12) Hearing and vision screening requirements (18) Promotion of indoor and outdoor physical activity (E) (F) (G) (19) Procedures for providing and applying, as needed, insect repellant and sunscreen. (22) Procedures for parents to review a copy of the child-care center's most recent Licensing inspection report and how the parent may access the minimum standards online (23) Instructions on how a parent may contact the local Licensing office, access the Texas Abuse and Neglect Hotline, and access the HHSC website (24) Your emergency preparedness plan (26) Preventing and responding to abuse and neglect of children. (27) Procedures for conducting health checks, if applicable (28) Information on vaccine-preventable diseases for employees (29) If your operation administers unassigned epinephrine auto injectors to use in case of an emergency Anaphylaxis reaction. (30) Procedures for supporting inclusive services to children with special care needs.

The parent handbook did not contain procedure for parent notifications.  The operational policies were also missing the promotion of indoor/outdoor physical activities, procedures for parental notifications, and procedures for parent participation in operation's activities.

The operation's operational policies address communication between parents and the school which includes parental notifications, methods of communication, classrooms being equipped with a phone for efficient communication between staff and management, open communication between parents and the school being integral to Kids R Kids, contacting teachers, contacting management, and emergencies. Health checks and illness and injury are also addressed in the operational policies. It is important staff and management are following their operational policies as well as minimum standards regarding communicating with parents when applicable. Information gathered in the investigation substantiated there was a lapse of communication regarding an incident where a pre-k aged child had an accident and was changed into clean underwear but no bottoms as it was believed the child did not have extra clothes. The child was present at the operation for two to three hours with their underwear being visible with no dress or shorts/pants to cover the underwear. While a caregiver initially reached out to management there was no follow up from the caregiver or management in regard to the situation with each other or with the parent. The parent was not notified.
